title: Mitigate context-fragmentation-induced tokens/sec collapse in mixed workloads
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private have reported a sharp drop in tokens/sec (measured as sustained token throughput) during mixed small/long-context workloads after the 1.22 kernel scheduling change. Symptoms: steady TTFT for short single-turn requests but ~40-60% drop in sustained tokens/sec for multi-request streaming sessions and long-context priming patterns. Occurrence window: started 2026-03-09 after rollout of kernel heuristic v1.22. Impact: production requests see prolonged completion times, customers report timeouts and increased cost due to longer GPU occupancy. Affected stacks: NVidia A100 and H100 pools with mixed-precision quantized models (int8/qat experiments), observed in Hosted auto-pool, one Dedicated cluster, and two Private installs behind customer-managed routers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a model in runtime-1.22 with int8 quantization and mixed-length request workload (prefill heavy + many short follow-ups).
2) Send parallel streaming sessions (50-100) mixing prefill length 1k tokens and frequent short asks (5-20 tokens) at 60-120 rps aggregate.
3) Observe tokens/sec on the worker aggregator and per-GPU metrics: TX rate drops after ~45s and stays ~40-60% below baseline; TTFT remains near normal for single small requests.
4) Repro on Private by running the customer workload harness in staging (links below).
root_cause_summary: Preliminary RCA: a combination of (a) the new kernel selection heuristic favoring low-latency single-request kernels that disable continuous KV cache concatenation across microbatches; (b) fragmentation of attention plan allocations when context windows alternate between long and short, causing buffer churn and cross-tenant memory thrash; and (c) an interaction with the prefill handshake timeout that causes the batching pipeline to force smaller microbatches for several seconds after large prefills. Together these reduce effective tokens/s even though first-token latency remains acceptable for short requests.
proposed_fix: Short-term: implement a runtime circuit that detects mixed-length session patterns and forces 'concat-friendly' kernel selection and KV cache sticky residency for 60s after a large prefill. This is a config-guarded hotfix (runtime flag: runtime.concat_fallback=true) to be deployed to Hosted autoscaler, Dedicated kube pool, and provided as an ops playbook + patch for Private customers. Long-term: rework kernel heuristic to incorporate session-level signals, add buffer reservation to avoid fragmentation, and extend prefill handshake to avoid microbatch collapse.
rollout_plan: 1) Create feature-gated hotfix branch (runtime-hotfix/concat-fallback) and run full perf regression suite.
2) Deploy to canary subset of Hosted (5% of traffic) + one Dedicated cluster; monitor tokens/sec, queue depth, and GPU memory churn for 1 hour.
3) If canary stable, promote to 50% then 100% across Hosted, then coordinate Dedicated and Private downstream patches.
4) For Private customers, prepare backport patch and ops instructions; offer assistance for urgent installs.
5) Publish postmortem and update kernel selection docs.
verification_criteria: Sustained tokens/sec for mixed workloads returns to within 95% of pre-rollout baseline over a 10-minute window.
No regressions in single-request TTFT (first-byte within 5% of baseline).
GPU memory churn and allocator fragmentation metrics show >30% reduction relative to failing state.
No increased OOMs or handshake timeouts observed in 1 hour after rollout.
Customer confirmation from two engaged escalations (support tickets linked) that behavior is resolved.
